description: Held-out U.S. history fact-check benchmark for calibrating relevance + entailment thresholds. Each case carries era/claim_type/difficulty metadata so the benchmark is reviewable and extensible. Every claim is sourced from widely cited U.S. history references; review_notes describe the rationale for the label.

cases.claim: The Mayflower arrived at Plymouth in 1620.
cases.statement: Mayflower voyage arrival year: 1620; landing site Plymouth.
cases.review_notes: Statement gives the same arrival year and location as the claim.

cases.claim: The Mayflower arrived at Plymouth in 1620.
cases.statement: Mayflower voyage arrival year: 1602.
cases.review_notes: Same event but the year is transposed; lexical overlap is high so this is a useful trap for the heuristic.

cases.claim: The United States Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
cases.statement: Declaration of Independence adoption date: July 4, 1776.
cases.review_notes: Direct match on entity and year.

cases.claim: The United States Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
cases.statement: Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1789 alongside the Bill of Rights.
cases.review_notes: Confuses adoption with later constitutional events; year mismatch.

cases.claim: The U.S. Constitution was ratified in 1788.
cases.statement: Constitution of the United States ratification year: 1788 (New Hampshire ninth state).
cases.review_notes: Standard ratification year confirmed by ninth-state milestone.

cases.claim: The U.S. Constitution was ratified in 1788.
cases.statement: U.S. Constitution was drafted in 1776 at the Continental Congress.
cases.review_notes: Wrong year and conflates Declaration-era drafting with Constitutional Convention.

cases.claim: The Louisiana Purchase occurred in 1803.
cases.statement: Louisiana Purchase signing year: 1803; territory acquired from France.
cases.review_notes: Year and counterparty both align with claim.

cases.claim: The Louisiana Purchase occurred in 1803.
cases.statement: Louisiana Purchase took place in 1903.
cases.review_notes: Wrong century; same entity.

cases.claim: The Indian Removal Act became law in 1830.
cases.statement: Indian Removal Act enactment year: 1830 under President Andrew Jackson.
cases.review_notes: Year plus executive context corroborate.

cases.claim: The U.S. Civil War ended in 1865.
cases.statement: American Civil War end time: 1865.
cases.review_notes: Standard textbook end date.

cases.claim: The U.S. Civil War ended in 1865.
cases.statement: American Civil War start time: 1861.
cases.review_notes: Right war, wrong endpoint of the date range.

cases.claim: The Emancipation Proclamation was issued in 1863.
cases.statement: Emancipation Proclamation issuance date: January 1, 1863.
cases.review_notes: Exact issuance date supports the year-level claim.

cases.claim: The Emancipation Proclamation was issued in 1863.
cases.statement: Emancipation Proclamation was issued in 1963.
cases.review_notes: Year typo trap.

cases.claim: The Thirteenth Amendment abolished slavery in 1865.
cases.statement: Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution ratification date: December 1865; effect: abolition of slavery and involuntary servitude.
cases.review_notes: Both effect and year align with claim.

cases.claim: The Thirteenth Amendment abolished slavery in 1865.
cases.statement: Thirteenth Amendment guaranteed women's voting rights.
cases.review_notes: Wrong amendment effect; the Nineteenth Amendment did that.

cases.claim: The 19th Amendment was ratified in 1920.
cases.statement: Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution ratification date: 1920.
cases.review_notes: Direct match.

cases.claim: The 19th Amendment was ratified in 1920.
cases.statement: Nineteenth Amendment introduced federal income taxation.
cases.review_notes: Confuses with Sixteenth Amendment; same numeric era but different scope.

cases.claim: The New Deal began in the 1930s.
cases.statement: New Deal period: 1933 to 1939.
cases.review_notes: Date range falls inside the 1930s decade.

cases.claim: The New Deal began in the 1930s.
cases.statement: The New Deal was a foreign policy treaty signed in 1945.
cases.review_notes: Wrong scope (foreign-policy treaty) and wrong era.

cases.claim: The U.S. entered World War II after Pearl Harbor in 1941.
cases.statement: Attack on Pearl Harbor date: 1941; U.S. declaration of war followed.
cases.review_notes: Causal chain (attack -> declaration) aligns with claim.

cases.claim: The U.S. entered World War II after Pearl Harbor in 1941.
cases.statement: Pearl Harbor was attacked in 1914.
cases.review_notes: Wrong decade for the attack.

cases.claim: The Marshall Plan was signed into law in 1948.
cases.statement: Marshall Plan (Economic Recovery Act) enactment date: April 1948.
cases.review_notes: Confirmed by formal program name and enactment month.

cases.claim: The Marshall Plan was signed into law in 1948.
cases.statement: Marshall Plan was an executive directive enacted in 1968.
cases.review_notes: Wrong enactment vehicle and wrong year.

cases.claim: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 outlawed discriminatory voting practices.
cases.statement: Voting Rights Act of 1965 enactment year: 1965; scope: federal prohibition on race-based voting discrimination.
cases.review_notes: Same year and same scope language.

cases.claim: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 outlawed discriminatory voting practices.
cases.statement: Voting Rights Act of 1965 created the Social Security Administration.
cases.review_notes: Wrong scope; SSA was created by the 1935 Social Security Act.

cases.claim: Apollo 11 landed astronauts on the Moon in 1969.
cases.statement: Apollo 11 Moon landing date: July 20, 1969.
cases.review_notes: Direct match on year and event.

cases.claim: Apollo 11 landed astronauts on the Moon in 1969.
cases.statement: Apollo 11 launched in 1959 and orbited Venus.
cases.review_notes: Wrong year and wrong destination.

cases.claim: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 banned segregation in public accommodations.
cases.statement: Civil Rights Act of 1964 scope: prohibits discrimination in public accommodations and employment.
cases.review_notes: Statement broadens scope but still entails the claim.

cases.claim: The United States co-founded NATO in 1949.
cases.statement: North Atlantic Treaty Organization founding year: 1949; United States among founding members.
cases.review_notes: Year and founding membership both align.

cases.claim: The United States co-founded NATO in 1949.
cases.statement: NATO was established in 1991 to replace the Warsaw Pact.
cases.review_notes: Year wrong and conflates with the end of the Cold War.
